title: Inventory and Interior
premise: Coral Hartwell has spent fifteen years as a night librarian, cataloguing other people's lives while keeping her own in storage. When her estranged mother's house—the one where Coral's brother Danny drowned the summer they were sixteen—goes to auction, she returns to inventory its contents and finds her mother's diaries, which reveal that what the family called an accident was witnessed, and silenced, by someone still living among them. As the auction date closes in and her siblings circle with their own claims on the past, Coral must decide whether exposing the truth will save or shatter the only family she has left. She chooses truth at the closing table, losing the house but finally owning herself.
about_author: Coral Underhill worked for a decade as a night-shift archivist in a coastal city before turning to fiction full-time. Her writing explores how families curate their own histories, and what survives when the records are finally opened.

chapters.title: The Night Stack
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet her reshelving books at 3 a.m., invisible by design, dodging a coworker's invitation to anything resembling a life. A certified letter arrives: the Hartwell house enters probate auction in six weeks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference; she tells no one.

chapters.title: Certified Mail
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She reads the auction notice forty times without opening the attached inventory list. Flashbacks establish the family arrangement: mother Marianne, older brother Theo who left first, and the silence around Danny's drowning. Beat: the past knocking like weather against glass.

chapters.title: Theo Answers on the Second Ring
chapters.summary: Coral calls Theo, now a real estate developer in another state, expecting refusal. He surprises her: he wants the house sold fast and clean, no ceremony. His briskness reads as grief management. Beat: two siblings negotiating around a locked room neither will name.

chapters.title: Return to Salt Row
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She drives back to the coastal town, checks into a motel, and stands outside the house unable to use her key. Neighbor Ruthie recognizes her instantly—small towns keep ledgers too. Beat: the vertigo of being seen after years of anonymity.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Coral catalogs the house room by room, professionally, using librarian's discipline as armor. Each object triggers memory: Danny's swim trophies, the patched screen door, Marianne's locked desk drawer. Beat: order imposed on chaos, holding something worse at bay.

chapters.title: The Desk Drawer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She picks the drawer lock and finds eleven years of Marianne's diaries plus a coroner's report she was never shown. The report notes Danny had bruising inconsistent with drowning alone. Beat: the floor tilting; her invisibility suddenly feels complicit.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Remembers
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Over pie, the neighbor recalls the summer of the drowning: three kids at the quarry, not two, and Marianne paying off a boat owner within the month. Ruthie has kept quiet for decades out of loyalty. Beat: the town's own architecture of silence exposed.

chapters.title: Theo Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Theo shows up unannounced, ostensibly to help stage the house, really to control the timeline. He notices the diaries are missing from the drawer and goes very still. Beat: sibling chess begins; love and leverage indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Diary of August 1989
chapters.summary: Excerpts from Marianne's diary, framed by Coral reading aloud alone at night. Marianne knew what happened at the quarry and chose the family's survival over justice, recording her bargain in increasingly fractured prose. Beat: Coral recognizing her own silence as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Third Child
chapters.summary: Coral confronts the impossible detail: there were three kids at the quarry, and she was one of them—but she remembers nothing. Dr. Okafor, a local therapist, suggests dissociative amnesia. Beat: the horror that she may be the witness her family arranged itself around.

chapters.title: Auction Preview
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the public preview she watches strangers appraise her childhood, including a young couple charmed by the porch where Danny once taught her card tricks. She nearly warns them off. Beat: grief weaponized into protectiveness; the house is not just property.

chapters.title: Theo's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo proposes Coral sign a waiver releasing any claim and hand over the diaries; in exchange he'll buy the house himself and 'keep it in the family.' The offer is generous and a cage. Beat: loyalty priced in square footage; Coral sees the transaction clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: Marianne's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The final diary entry, written weeks before Marianne's death, names the person responsible for Danny's death—and asks Coral's forgiveness for what she did to keep it buried. Beat: devastation and strange relief; the question has been waiting for her all along.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Quarry
chapters.summary: Coral brings Theo to the quarry at dusk and reads the entry aloud. He breaks—not with confession but with fury, then collapse: it was an accident during a dare gone wrong, and he was fourteen and terrified. Beat: rising action cresting; truth and blame refusing to separate cleanly.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Ledger Closes
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie admits she took money from Marianne to stay silent about seeing Theo run from the water. Now elderly and unafraid, she tells Coral she'll testify to whatever Coral decides. Beat: the cost of survival made concrete; loyalty examined and found wanting.

chapters.title: The Night Before Closing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sleepless in the motel, she drafts and discards three versions of what she'll do: sign, burn the diaries, or speak. A call from the young couple who lost their bid on the house gives her an unexpected image of the future. Beat: the eye of the storm; choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Closing Table
chapters.summary: Climax. At the escrow office, with Theo, the buyers' agent, and a notary present, Coral reads Marianne's final entry instead of signing quietly. Theo walks out; the sale proceeds anyway because the house sells regardless of what is said. Beat: truth spoken at last, and its price paid in full view.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Salt Row
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The town reacts in ripples—some grateful, some vicious. Theo stops returning calls. Ruthie sits with her on the porch of the empty house one last time. Beat: the loneliness of honesty, and the first breath of air that isn't borrowed.

chapters.title: What the House Sold For
chapters.summary: Coral learns Theo bought the house through a shell company before the auction even closed—he wanted it erased, not kept. She mails him the diaries' originals, keeping only scans. Beat: relinquishing control of the evidence; trust offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: Reshelving
chapters.summary: Back at the library, Coral requests a transfer to the day shift—a small revolution. She begins a finding aid for the family papers, treating her history as an archive worth preserving rather than sealing. Beat: transformation enacted in professional ritual; ownership replacing tenancy.

chapters.title: Danny's Porch
chapters.summary: Coral visits the new owners, who invite her in; the wife found Danny's card deck in a kitchen drawer and asks if she'd teach them the trick. On the porch, Coral performs it badly and laughs until she cries. Beat: grief integrated; memory handed forward instead of hidden.

chapters.title: Owner of Record
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Coral's POV. Months later, Theo sends a single letter: no apology, but a photograph of the house and the words 'I remember him too.' Coral pins it above her desk. She is no longer a tenant of her own life. Beat: resolution without absolution; the question answered, the price acknowledged, survival redefined.
